en: May that Sun, the lamp of the three worlds with his manifold rays, grant us speech in the Veda—he who is conceived as the various divisions of the zodiac and as the embodied form of the moon; who is the path for those who are not born again; who is the Self for the knowers of the Self; who is the sacrifice for those who perform rituals; who is the Lord of the immortal lights; and who is the omnipresent power in many ways over the dissolution, creation, and maintenance of the worlds. (Śālivāhana-vijaya)

Although many treatises endowed with grammar and logic have been studied by those of sharp intellect for the sake of making known the results of horā, I— whose efforts have failed in crossing the great ocean of the *horā-tantra*— here begin a small boat of a manual that is diverse in verse and rich in meaning. (Śā.vi) Some desire that *horā* refers to the division of day and night (*aho-rātra-vikalpa*), due to the elision of the first and last letters.

It manifests the sequence of that [karma] which was acquired through actions in previous existences, beginning with the present life. (Indravajrā) Time, the limbs, the excellent limb, the face, the chest, the heart, the belly, the garment, the bladder, the genitals, the thighs, the pair of knees, the shanks, and then the pair of feet;

the nine constellations beginning with Aries and Gemini are the feet; the zodiac signs situated on the wheel; "sign," "field," "house," "constellation," "asterism," and "abode" are synonyms for the same thing. (Śālinī)
The Fish, the Jar, the Man, the Couple with the mace, the Couple with the lute, the Archer-man, the Horse-hipped woman, the Crocodile, the Deer-faced woman,
the Balance with grain and fire, and the Maiden with the monkey— all these [signs] correspond to their own names, and all are mobile.
Mars, Venus, Mercury, the Moon, the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Rahu, and Jupiter are the lords of the houses and their respective degrees.

The rule for the nine *navāṃśas* begins with the goat (*aja*), deer (*mṛga*), balance (*tuli*), and moon (*candra*) signs; the lords of these *aṃśakas* are the same as those of the signs themselves, starting from their own houses in sequence. (Troṭaka) The portions belong to Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus, corresponding to the signs of Wind (Aries), Air (Gemini), Crab, Balance, and Fish. In odd signs, however, they are situated in reverse order; in even signs, the junctions of the asterisms end at the Moon sign, Libra, and Pisces. (Puṣpitāgrā)

Kriya, Tāvuri, Jituma, Kulīra, Leya, Pāthona, Jūka, Kaurpya, Taukṣika, Ākokera, Hṛdroga, and Antyabha— thus [are the names of the signs]. The designations Dreṣkāṇa, Horā, Navabhāga, Triṃśāṃśaka, and Dvādaśāṃśaka are also [to be known].
The field of a sign is its own division, while the *horā* is half of the sign or the ascendant.
Taurus, Aries, Capricorn, Cancer, and Gemini, along with Capricorn, are called nocturnal signs; those same signs, excluding Gemini, are said to be "rising from the back" (*pṛṣṭhodaya*).

The remaining [planets] possess the strength of their respective signs of exaltation on the day; the ascendant, meeting both [the Sun and Moon], possesses a pair of broad brows. (Vasantatilakā) Male and female [planets] are the cruel and the gentle; they are the moving and the fixed, and the dual-bodied [planets]. The lords of the directions starting from the East are Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer, along with their trines. The *horās* belong to the Sun and Moon in odd and even signs respectively; the *dreṣkāṇas* belong to the Moon, the Sun, and the lords of the domicile, the fifth house, and the trine houses. (Mandākrāntā)
Some, however, desire the first *horā* for the lord of the [natal] sign, and the second for the lord of the eleventh house;
they also describe the designation of *dreṣkāṇas* as belonging to the lords of one's own twelfth and eleventh signs.
(Indravajrā) Aries, Taurus, Capricorn, Virgo, Cancer, Pisces, and Libra are the exaltations (*tuṅga*) of the Sun and the other planets respectively.
The signs Leo, Taurus, Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Aquarius are the exaltations of the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rahu, and Ketu respectively.
(Puṣpitāgrā) The nine divisions known as *varga-uttama*, *cara-gṛha-ādi*, and so forth—beginning from the first and ending with the middle—are auspicious in their respective results.
(Vasantatilakā) Leo, Taurus, Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Aquarius are the trines (tri-kona) from the Sun. (Vasantatilakā)
The house, family, siblings, kinsmen, children, enemies, wife, death, auspicious stations, and income—these are the houses beginning with the Ascendant (Horā).
Those known as the "expenditure" (Riṣpha), the "upacaya" (beneficial) houses, and those termed the enemy, action, gain, and difficult (Duścikya) are not always so, according to some authorities.
Rituals, one's own prowess, home, intelligence, injury, mental anguish, loss, teacher, honor, birth, and expenditure—these are the houses beginning with the Second (Sva).

The fourth and eighth houses from the ascendant are known as the quadrants (caturasra), while the seventh house is called the dyūna and the tenth house is the ājñā. The seventh, the ascendant, the fourth, and the tenth are designated as the angles (kaṇṭaka) and the four centers (kendracatuṣṭaya). Within these aforementioned positions, the signs of quadrupeds (kīṭa), humans (nara), water-dwellers (ambu-cara), and animals (paśu) are respectively endowed with strength.

From the ascendant (kendram), the next is the quadrant (paṇapharam); beyond that, all signs are semi-quadrants (āpoklimam). The fourth house (hibukam) is the water-house (ambu) and the house of happiness (sukham). The seventh house (jāmitram) is the house of setting (astabhavanam). One should know the tenth house (daśamam) here as the trine (trikoṇam) and the house of exertion (meṣūraṇam), as well as the house of action (karma). The lords of the horās, Jupiter, and Mercury—when conjoined with or aspected by these, and not by others; when situated in angles (kendras) and possessing intense strength; and when the two-footed signs and so forth are placed in them during the day, the night, or at both twilights.

In the first half [of the zodiac], the objects and so forth, the qualities performed, the measure, the contrary, that which is difficult to pierce, the innate, austerity, and the ninth—the third and so on, the trine, and that [are the signs] (Śā.vi).

Red, white, resembling the body of a parrot, pale-red, smoky, pale-yellow, variegated, black, like gold, tawny, speckled, brown, and clear—these are the colors in the first houses from the beginning (Maṃ.krāṃ). Jumping, the direction of the lord, and the "approacher" (veśi) from the sign joined with the sun, and the second [from it] (E1).

The planets represent: the divisions of time, the soul, the sun, the mind, the moon, the quality of *sattva*, Mars, wisdom, speech, Jupiter, knowledge and happiness, Venus, passion, suffering, and the son of the Lord of Day (Saturn).
The Sun and the Moon are kings; Mars is a leader; Mercury is a prince; Jupiter is honored by the Dānavas; and Venus is a minister; while the thousand-rayed one (the Sun) is a servant. (Śa.vi)
Heli, Sūrya, Candramas, Śītarashmi; Hemna, Vijña, Bodhana, Induputra; Āra, Vakra, Krūradṛk, Avaneya, Koṇa, Manda, Sūryaputra, Asita;
Jīva, Aṅgiras, Suraguru, Vacasāmpati, Ijya, Śukra, Bhṛgu, Bhṛgusuta, Sita, Āsphujit. (Śālinī meter)

Rāhu is Tamas, Aguru, and Asura; Ketu is Śikhin—having learned these other synonyms, one may speak of them according to worldly usage. (Vaṃśastha) The Sun is red and dark; the Moon is fair-complexioned and not very tall; Mars is reddish-fair; Mercury is dark like dūrvā grass; Jupiter has a fair body; Venus is dark; and Saturn has a black body. (Śālinī)

The colors are copper, white, deep red, green, yellow, variegated, and black. The many lords of the planets in order are those born of water, fire, Keśava (Viṣṇu), Indra, Śacī, Sūrya, and so forth. Starting from the east, they are the Sun, Venus, Mars, Rāhu, Saturn, the Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, the waning Moon, the Sun, Earth’s son (Mars), the Sun’s son (Saturn)—the malefics—and Mercury joined with them. Mercury and Saturn are called neuter; the Moon and Venus are females; and the remaining [planets] are males. (Śārṅgadharapaddhati)
The lords of the groups of fire, earth, ether, water, and wind are, in order, Mars and the others [Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn].
(Troṭaka) Starting from the Brahmin, [the lords of the castes] are Venus, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, the Moon, and Mercury; these belong to the Śūdras and the outcastes.
(Upajātikā) The Moon, the Sun, Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, Mars, and Saturn are, respectively, the qualities of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. (Upajātikā)
The Sun has honey-brown eyes, a square body, a bilious temperament, and sparse hair;
the Moon has a slender, round body, an abundance of wind and phlegm, is wise, soft-spoken, and possesses auspicious eyes.
(Troṭaka meter) Mars has a cruel gaze, a youthful form, is noble, bilious, very fickle, and thin-waisted.

One who speaks with puns, always delights in laughter, is wise, and possesses a temperament of bile, wind, and phlegm; (in the Svāgatā meter) one who has a large body, reddish-brown hair and eyes, is Bṛhaspati, of excellent intellect, and of a phlegmatic nature;
Bhṛgu is happy, of lovely form and beautiful eyes, of a phlegmatic and windy nature, with dark face and hair. (In the Vaṃśastha meter)
The [planets] beginning with Mars are respectively: dull, lazy, tawny-eyed, thin and tall-bodied, thick-toothed, coarse-haired and bearded, and having wind as their nature;

they consist of sinews, bones, blood, skin, semen, fat, marrow, and the Moon; and they rule over the gods, water, fire, recreation, the treasury, the bed, the earth, and the rubbish heap. Their respective cloths are: coarse, unwashed, burnt by fire, middling, firm, and torn.

Copper, gems, gold, silver, iron, and pearls correspond to the Sun and the other planets respectively; or else, the seasons beginning with winter (Śiśira) correspond to the signs starting from Aries as they rise through the decans (dreṣkāṇas). The Sun, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, and the others look upon the trines (3rd and 9th), the angles (1st and 7th), and the quadrants (4th and 8th) with increasing degrees of aspectual strength. Indeed, these planets become progressively more powerful in their aspects in that order.
From the Sun [proceed] the solstices, moments, days, seasons, months, fortnights, and years;
and [the tastes] pungent, salty, bitter, mixed, sweet, sour, and astringent. (In the Vaitālīya meter:
Jīva, Jīva, Budha, Śita, Indutanaya, and those excluding Arka and Vibhūma are, in order, friends to Vīndu, Arkā, Vikuja, Indvin, and Īna—such is the opinion of some.

When truth is spoken, from one's own trine house, the lords of the fifth, ninth, and second houses, as well as the lords of the tenth, eleventh, fourth, and seventh houses, are friends according to their own specific characteristics; they do not become enemies through other factors.

(Śāravi) For the Sun, Mars and Saturn are enemies, Venus is neutral, and Mercury is a friend; the remaining planets are neutral. For the Moon, the Sun and Mercury are friends, while the others are neutral. For Mars, Jupiter, the Moon, and the Sun are friends, Mercury is an enemy, and Venus and Saturn are neutral. For Mercury, the Sun and Venus are friends, the Moon is an enemy, and the others are neutral. (Śāravi)

The Sun, Mercury, and Venus are friendly; the Son of the Sun (Saturn) is neutral; and the others are otherwise. Mercury and the Sun are friends to Jupiter; Mars and Saturn are neutral; and the remaining planets are enemies. To Saturn, Venus and Mars are friends; Jupiter is neutral; and the others are enemies. Those who have been declared as such in their own signs, trines, and so forth, have now been proclaimed by me once again [in this specific context]. (Śāravi) When they occupy each other's second, twelfth, eleventh, third, tenth, or fourth houses at that time, they are friends; even if they are in their own exaltation signs, some are otherwise [enemies].

Having considered the planets as neutral, friends, equals, and enemies according to their natural (naisargika) relationships, one should again determine them as super-friends, friends, and so forth for that specific time.
(Śāravi) Planetary positional strength (*sthānabala*) is derived from being in its own sign, exaltation, a friend's sign, its own trine, its own navāṃśa, or having entered its own domicile.
In the directions [starting from the east], Mercury and Jupiter, the Sun and Mars, Saturn, Venus, and the Moon are situated respectively. (Dodhaka)
At the northern solstice, the Sun and the Moon are retrograde; the remaining planets are in conjunction with them.
Those situated in the northern hemisphere should be understood as possessing great power in battle, endowed with activity and heroism.

(Dodhaka meter) At night, the Moon, Mars, and Saturn [are strong]; Mercury is always so; and the others [Jupiter, Venus, and Rahu] are so during the day. Cruel and gentle planets are respectively situated in the dark and bright fortnights.

The strength of time is determined by the two solstices, the day, the hour, and the months; [the planets] beginning with the Sun, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus possess strength through their increase. Birth in a non-natal sign occurs when malefic planets are very strong, benefic planets are weak, and the Moon is situated in a quadrangle or through its aspect upon it.

If the *sattva* (the sum of the strengths of the planets) should be equal in form to the two-fold portion associated with the Moon, one should declare that person to be known as "born of a womb" (*viyoni*). (Va.Ti.
Malefics are strong when situated in their own divisions, while they are weak in the divisions of others; benefics are the opposite.
Having observed that the ascendant is designated as "born of a womb," one should likewise predict a "womb-born" [offspring] even in this case. (Vai.Lī.)
The head, face, neck, shoulders, other [parts], the feet, portions, the back, the chest, and then the sides;
the belly, the anus, the legs, then the genitals, the testicles, the buttocks, and the tail—thus he has described the limbs of quadrupeds.
(Ujjvalā) One should declare the colors from the conjunction or aspect of planets starting from the degree of the ascendant, provided they are endowed with strength, in the case of two-footed beings.

One should declare [the number of] birds equal to the [number of] aspects, or state the lines according to their own count; and on the back [of the horoscope], by means of those situated in the Smara [seventh house].

(Vaiśvadevī meter) When the bird-sign (Khaga-dṛkāṇa) is joined with a planet endowed with strength, or at the rising of a movable sign or its divisions, or in the division of Mercury, there are birds and land-lotuses (aquatic creatures) produced by the yoga of the aspect of Saturn and the Moon. (Vaṃśastha meter)

When the ruler of the hour (horā), the Moon, Jupiter, and the Sun are strong, there is a distinction based on the signs occupied by the planets at birth: those born in water-signs produce trees for water, and those in land-signs produce trees for land. Furthermore, from the Ascendant, however many planets there are that rule over land or water signs, that many trees will grow, whether on land or in water. (Vṛtta-taraṅgiṇī) The Sun produces trees with internal sap; the Son of the Sun (Saturn) produces unfortunate ones; the Moon produces those endowed with milky sap; and Mars produces those rich in thorns.

Venus [rules] speech, Jupiter [rules] the intellect, and Saturn [rules] fruit-bearing and fruitless trees; Venus [also rules] flowering trees, while the Moon [rules] lush ones, and Mars [rules] trees with pungent branches.
A benefic planet situated in a benefic asterism produces a beautiful tree born of good soil, whereas the opposite occurs otherwise.
In the *para-aṃśaka* (the portion belonging to another), however many [degrees] one has fallen from one's own [portion], there will be trees of that same kind. (Vaṃśastha meter) E3.
The cause for conception is Mars and the Moon; when the monthly menses occurs, it should be examined whether the Moon has entered a painful asterism (*pīḍa-ṛkṣa*).
Otherwise, if the seventh house is occupied by or aspected by auspicious male planets, the woman enters into union with the man.
Just as the sign of Libra (the Balance) comes together with Gemini (the Twins), so too should the sexual union be described.
If the seventh house is conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets, the union is full of anger; if it is conjoined with or aspected by benefics, it is full of playful smiles.

When the Sun, Moon, Venus, and Mars occupy their own signs and Jupiter is situated in a trine or in the ascendant, offspring indeed arise even for those who are "seedless" (barren); yet these [planets] are as fruitless as the rays of the moon to those with defective eyes. When the Sun and Moon are in the seventh house and Mars and Saturn are there, then disease is brought to the man and the woman alike.
If [the Sun and Venus] are conjoined in the twelfth or second house, they cause death; likewise, if they are aspected by one another, they are ordained for death.
(Vaṃśastha meter) During the day, the Sun and Venus are designated as the father and mother, while Saturn and the Moon are so designated at night; this is reversed during the night.
Furthermore, these two are designated as the paternal uncle and maternal aunt respectively when situated in odd and even asterisms, and they are auspicious in those positions. (Vaṃśastha meter)

When Saturn is joined with the ascendant sign, aspected by the Moon and Mars, and by malefics longing for the rising asterism while not receiving a benefic aspect, death occurs. (Vaṃśastha meter) When the ascendant and the Moon are situated between two malefics and are not aspected by benefics, [death follows].
A woman who speaks either simultaneously or separately [with her husband] perishes while pregnant.

(Vaitālīya) If Mars is in the fourth house from the Moon or from the ascendant, or if it is situated in the eighth house, and the waning Moon is in the fifth or twelfth house, death occurs as previously described. (Vaitālīya)
If Mars and the Sun are at their rising and setting [respectively], one should predict death caused by weapons;
likewise, if the lord of the month is afflicted, one should indicate hemorrhaging at that time.
(Vaidyanātha Līlāvatī) When benefic planets occupy the Moon-sign ascendant and are situated in the trines, the seventh house, the second house, or the fourth house, [they bestow prosperity].
If malefic planets are situated in the third, the eleventh, and the eighth houses, yet the embryo is aspected by the Sun, it shall be healthy.

(Vaṃśastha meter) One should declare the birth of a male when the Ascendant, the Sun, Jupiter, and the Moon are strong and occupy odd signs and masculine divisions (*puruṣa-aṃśaka*); and the birth of a female when they occupy even signs and neutral divisions (*sama-aṃśaka*).

Jupiter and the Sun in an odd sign produce a male; the Moon and Venus in an odd sign, or Mars in an even sign, produce a female. Furthermore, through the aspect of Mercury situated in two signs, they cause twins within their own respective periods. (Śārdūlavikrīḍita meter)
Even Saturn, situated in an odd sign and having left the ascendant, causes the birth of a male from the ascendant;

Even when the Moon and Mercury are situated in even or odd signs, if they are aspected by Mars; and when Venus, the Ascendant, and the Moon—these six—are in male signs; these are recorded as the "neuter" (klība) yogas.

(Śārṅgadharapaddhati) If the Moon and Venus are in an even sign, or if Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, and the Ascendant are in odd houses; or if the Ascendant and the Moon are conjoined and aspected by a male planet in even signs, they produce a male being.

These planets, having reached the Ascendant, form a couple when they aspect two limbs or degrees in their own division (svāṃśa). When Mercury aspects three [degrees] by virtue of its own division, a couple is formed; however, by unmixed [planets], it is equal [to the previous]. (Śārṅgadharapaddhati)

When the ascendant is at the end of the Dhanus (Sagittarius) sign, and it is aspected by powerful planets situated in its own degrees—specifically by Mercury and Saturn endowed with strength—even abundant wealth existing in the treasury is lost.

The stages of the embryo—kalala, ghana, aṅkura, asthi, carma, aṅgaja, and cetanatā—are presided over respectively by Venus, Mars, Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, Saturn, and Mercury. Beyond these [stages] are the others.

The lords of the rising sign, the Moon, and the Sun are declared in sequence to produce auspicious or inauspicious results according to the nature of the lord of the month. (Kuṭaka) If Mercury is in a trine with weak or other planets, and is situated in the mouth, feet, or hands, then the result shall be doubled. If the Moon is in the lower part of the zodiac and aspected by benefics while occupying a junction between signs (*bhasandhi*), it produces speech only after a long time. (Vaṃśastha)

If Saturn and Mars are in a benefic nakṣatra and its portion, one born there will have protruding teeth; if the Moon is in its own nakṣatra in the ascendant and aspected by Saturn and Mars, one will be hunchbacked.

If Pisces is in the ascendant and aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and Mars, one will be lame; if a malefic is at the junction [of a sign] and the Moon is there, one will be dull-witted, unless it is aspected by a benefic.
If the ascendant is Pisces, the last degree, and aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, one will be a dwarf.
If the Drekāṇas situated in the ninth and ninth-from-the-ninth houses (the fifth and eleventh) from the ascendant are joined by malefic planets, one will be without arms, legs, or head.
If Leo is the ascendant joined by the Sun and Moon and aspected by Mars and Saturn, one is eyeless; with benefic and malefic planets [so placed], one has eyes like bubbles.
The Moon situated in the twelfth house destroys the left [eye], and the Sun destroys the other; those configurations declared inauspicious become remediable if they are aspected by benefics.
At that time, when the Moon is joined with a portion of two rasas (twenty-four degrees), and the Moon is situated in a sign equal to that [portion] ahead,
birth is said to occur at the point where an equal division of day and night has elapsed.
If the delivery occurs when the Moon is rising in a soft sign (mṛdu-bha) and Saturn is in the seventh house, birth takes place after three years.
This procedure for the moon [ceremony] should be performed in the twelfth year; what has been stated here should be considered with reason even at the time of birth. (Mālinī) E4:
For a father who is absent when the son is born, the rite of birth [should be done] when the moon is visible in the ascendant.

When the sun has deviated from the middle of the sign occupied by a planet situated in a foreign land (during its transit), or when Saturn or Mars is positioned at the ascendant, or when the Moon is situated between Rāhu and Venus; (10) or when Saturn or Mars has set, or when the Moon is situated between Mercury and Venus; (11) (Anuṣṭubh)

If the Moon is in a malefic ascendant, or if the lord of Scorpio occupies the third house, and the benefics are situated in their own signs, one born [under such conditions] becomes a snake, or even one encircled by snakes. When the Sun has entered a quadrupedal sign, and the remaining planets are endowed with strength, [the same result follows].

If [Saturn] is situated in two bodies (houses), twins are born wrapped in a sheath. (Anuṣṭubh) If Saturn or Mars is situated in Aries, Leo, or Taurus as the ascendant, the child is born with a body resembling the sign and its degree, encircled by a navel-cord. (No specific meter name)
If Jupiter does not aspect the ascendant or the Moon, or if the Moon is conjoined with the Sun;

or if the Moon is joined with a malefic or by another [planet], they declare from certainty that the person born is wicked. When two malefic planets are situated in inauspicious signs, located in the seventh, ninth, or fifth houses from the Sun.
If the father is bound, imprisoned, or traveling abroad, it is due to the influence of his own zodiac sign, or else while on a journey.
(Vaitālīya) When the full moon is in its own sign, a benefic planet is in the ascendant, and there is a benefic in the fourth house;
or when the moon is in the ascendant, in a watery sign, or in the seventh house, she gives birth while on a ship. (Vaitālīya)

If the Moon, situated in a watery sign, is full and aspects [the ascendant], or if it is in the ascendant belonging to a sign related to fish or rams, there will be birth in water; of this there is no doubt. (In the Vaitālīya meter:
If the Sun and Moon are in the twelfth house and Saturn, aspected by malefics, is in the eighth house...
If Saturn is in the ascendant conjoined with Ali-karki and aspected by the Moon, [the native] is born in a banyan tree.

(Vaitālīya meter) If Saturn is in the sign of Cancer in the ascendant and aspected respectively by Mercury, the Sun, and the Moon, he is born in a pleasure house, a temple, or on mountainous grounds. (Vaitālīya meter)

Seeing Mars situated in the human sign (Capricorn), he produces birth in a delightful cremation ground; Venus and the Moon in a fire-sacrifice; Jupiter among the families of kings, lords of men, or gods; the Sun in the dwellings of artisans;
and Mercury in a house that is movable, movable-in-aspect, or fixed. (Upajāti)

When a planet has reached its own asterism or its own Navāṃśa, the results of that asterism and that Navāṃśa arise through the conjunction of strength. (In the Vaitālīya meter) If the Moon is in a trine from Mars and Saturn, and is in its setting [decrepitude], the child is abandoned by the mother;
however, if it is aspected by the minister of the king of the gods (Jupiter), he is declared to possess long life and happiness. (In the Vaitālīya meter)

If Mars is aspected by a malefic at the time of the moon's rising, the child abandoned [at birth] perishes; the same applies if Mars and Saturn are in the eleventh house. Even if Mercury aspects them in such a manner, the child comes into the hands of others; if it is by any other [planet], even one gone into the hands of another, he does not live. By the strength of those [planets], the child may stay in the houses of his father or mother, or among trees, walls, and the like, when they are in their signs of debilitation.
If the ascendant and the Moon are not aspected by planets situated in the same sign, she gives birth in a secluded place.

(Vaitālīya) If the Moon is in a weak nakṣatra and degree, and is aspected by Saturn from the fourth house, or if Mars is there, or if Rāhu is conjoined with that [Mars] and situated in its sign of debilitation, the delivery occurs on the ground. Furthermore, whichever sign the Moon enters during the seventh house, the delivery of the fetus occurs accordingly. When malefics are situated in the seventh house from the Moon, they say there will be suffering for the mother. (Mandākrāntā)
Oil from the moon (the hare-mark), a wick from the rising (of the sun), and a lamp from the conjunction with the sun; movement and so forth from the influence of the stars;

and the door in that building—these are to be known by the planets situated in the angles (*kendras*) or endowed with strength. (*Indravajrā*) When Saturn is present, the house is old but renovated; when Mars, it is burnt; when the Moon, it is new; when the Sun, it is abundant in wood but not firm; when Mercury, it is not produced by a single craftsman but is beautiful.

When Venus is in the ninth house, the house is variegated; when Jupiter is there, it is a firm mansion. One should describe the construction according to the instructions of the *Cakra*, beginning with the neighboring regions.
(Śārṅgadharapaddhati) With Aries, Cancer, Libra, Scorpio, and Capricorn, the residence is in the east and north in the houses of Jupiter and Mercury;
with Taurus, it is in the west; and with Sagittarius and Leo, it is in the southern part. (Dodhaka)
In the houses starting from the East, the two activities (kriyā) and so forth are located in each pair of corners; these are the two-fold forms.
One should speak of the beds as well according to the Vāstu [rules], by means of the feet situated at six, three, nine, and the end. (In the Vaitālīya meter:
When the planets are situated between the Moon and the Ascendant, there will be female attendants (upasūtikā).

The [ascendant] is visible or invisible depending on whether it is within or outside half the circle [of the horizon], according to others. (Anuṣṭubh) The body [of the native] should be equal to the ninth-part (navāṃśa) of the ascendant, or its form should be like that of the planet endowed with strength;
its complexion is like that of the ninth-part occupied by the Moon, and its limbs are determined by the signs obtained by dividing the ascendant by twelve, starting from the letter *ka*. (Dodhaka)
The head, eyes, ears, nose, cheeks, jaws, and mouth; then the throat, shoulders, arms, sides, heart, chest, and navel;

then the bladder, penis, anus, testicles, thighs, knees, shanks, and feet—these are the parts for both [ascendants] in three divisions according to the degrees of the Drekkāṇas starting from the left. (Śā.vi) If that [part] is joined with a malefic, one should predict a wound; if joined with or aspected by a benefic, a mark or the like. If it is situated in its own asterism and degree, and in fixed signs, the birthmark is innate; otherwise, it is adventitious.

Fire-born [afflictions] arise from Mars, those from weapons and poison from Mercury; on Saturday, they arise from the earth, and on Wednesday, from the earth as well. On Sunday, they arise from wood or quadrupeds; on Monday, from horns; and on Tuesday, from water-born [sources]. By other [planets], there is auspiciousness. (Śārṅgadharapaddhati) In whichever portion three planets, including Mercury, are situated together, there will certainly be an occurrence therein, whether auspicious or inauspicious. An inauspicious planet causing a wound is located in the sixth house from the body [ascendant]; if it is situated in the same sign as the body [ascendant] and is repeatedly aspected by or conjoined with benefics, one becomes possessed of marks of fortune. (Hariṇī meter) E5

If at the time of the *ariṣṭa-sandhyā*, the Moon is in its period (*horā*) and the malefic planets are situated at the end of the sign, it leads to death; or if the Moon is joined by malefics in the seventh house, or if the malefics occupy the angles (*kendras*), that person meets with destruction. (Vidyunmālā)

If malefic or benefic planets are situated in the eastern or western halves of the zodiacal wheel during a Cancer ascendant, the native quickly meets with destruction; likewise, if malefics are positioned around both the ascendant and the setting point [the seventh house], the same occurs. (Indravajrā) Furthermore, if two malefics are situated at the rising and setting points [ascendant and seventh house] and the Moon is conjoined with a cruel planet...

And when death occurs before [the Moon] is aspected by benefics, it will happen before long. (Anuṣṭubh) When the Moon is waned and situated in the twelfth house, with malefics in the ascendant and the eighth house, and no benefics in the quadrants (kendras), one should declare that death will occur quickly. (Anuṣṭubh)

The Moon, conjoined with a malefic planet and situated in the seventh, twelfth, eighth, or ascendant houses, bestows death if it is not aspected by benefics from the *kaṇṭakas* (angular houses). (Anuṣṭubh) If the Moon is in the sixth or eighth house and aspected by malefics, death occurs quickly; however, if it is aspected by benefics, there is equality [of life and death], and if by mixed planets, there is stability.

If the lord of the ascendant is conjoined with benefics, aspected by strong benefics, situated in a favorable month, accompanied by its wife (the Moon), and victorious over malefics—[then there is no death].

(Pṛthvī meter) However, if the Moon is waning in the ascendant, and malefics occupy the eighth, the angles (kendras), or the interior [of the chart], and the Moon is situated in the eighth, the fourth, or the seventh house, [death occurs].

Thus, when the Ascendant is situated in Madana (the seventh house), and malefic planets are present there without being aspected by benefic planets capable of exerting power; (Mālinī/Mandākrāntā) When the Moon is at the end of its sign and not aspected by benefics, and malefics are positioned in the trines;
the infant quickly departs from life through the loss of breath. And when the malefics are in the setting [seventh] house and the Moon is in the Ascendant; (Indravajrā)

When the Moon is conjoined with or swallowed by a malefic planet and Mars is situated in the eighth house, there is death for the mother and son; however, if the Sun is in the ascendant, death results from a weapon.

When the Sun or the Moon is rising, if malefics endowed with strength occupy the trines and the eighth house, death occurs, provided they are neither conjoined with nor aspected by benefics. (In a *hariṇī* meter:
When Saturn, the Sun, the Moon, and Mars occupy the twelfth, ninth, first, and eighth houses respectively, [death follows].
Death quickly comes to embodied beings if [the Moon] is not aspected by a strong and powerful [planet].

(Aparavaktra) The Moon, joined with malefics in the fifth, seventh, twelfth, ascendant, or eighth houses, leads to death, unless it is conjoined with or aspected by Venus, Mercury, or Jupiter when they are strong. (Puṣpitāgrā)

When the strong Moon has gone to its own yoga-sthāna or to its own body-house (natal sign), and is aspected by malefic planets while being powerful, death indeed occurs within the year; so it was declared by the Sage. (Bhramaravilasitā meter) [This concerns] the allotment of lifespan.
The years for the Sun and other planets, beginning with Maya, Yavana, Maṇittha, and Śakti, are prescribed as follows:
nine, fifteen, twenty-four, eleven, eleven, and ten, when they are in their own exaltation signs.

From this, half is diminished when they are in their fall; for those situated between, there is proportionate calculation. Others say that the *horā* is equal to a degree, while others say it is equal to a sign.

Having abandoned the crookedness [of retrogression], one's own third part is diminished by the positions of the enemy planets; and when their luster is eclipsed by the Sun, Venus and Saturn lose half [of that]. (Mṛdaṅkāntā meter) Half, three-quarters, three-fourths, five-sixths, and six-sevenths are diminished from the house of expenditure (*vyayabhavana*) for malefics;
for benefics, it is half. Likewise, for those situated in the same sign, the strong planet takes away one degree. Thus spoke Satya. (Prahārṣiṇī meter)

When a malefic planet is conjoined with the ascendant, the total sum multiplied by nine and increased by seven-eighths undergoes destruction upon reaching a divisor of one hundred and eight; however, if it is aspected by a benefic according to this same rule, half of that [sum] goes to its end. For humans and elephants, sixty years doubled [is the lifespan]; for horses, five nights and five days; and for donkeys and young camels, the square of five [twenty-five years].

Even for a deformed person, the maximum lifespan is twelve years for a bull or a buffalo, ten for dogs, and sixteen for goats and the like. (Śikhariṇī) When the Moon’s son (Mercury) is situated in the sign of Taurus at its maximum degrees, and Jupiter is in the fifth house at five degrees, the measure of the maximum lifespan is indeed attained, provided all [planets] are in their own signs of exaltation. (Puṣpitāgrā)
Viṣṇugupta, Deva-svāmī, and Siddhasena have likewise composed [works on] the allotment of lifespan (*āyur-dāya*);
yet for them, a fault arises: excluding those with fatal signs (*ariṣṭa*), there would be no lifespan below twenty years.
(In the Śālinī meter) Regarding that yoga in which a full lifespan is prescribed, others declare that in that same case there is the status of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*).
This fault is evident; even another person lives out a full lifespan even without wealth.
(Śālinī meter) Jīvaśarman, it is said, stated according to his own view that the planetary allotment is a portion of the maximum lifespan.
That this is a true statement is supported by a great deal of consistency with the zodiacal signs and nine-divisional portions traversed by the planets. (Upacchandasikā meter)

When the true [longitude] is stated, the desired planet is converted into minutes; divided by two hundred, the quotient represents the years elapsed since the last revolution. From the remainder, the months and so forth are derived.

(Āryā verse) [The calculation is performed] for those [planets] that have reached their own apogees or retrograde motion; [the result is] tripled when they are in the second, highest, own, or third-quarter of their signs.
This much is the distinction in the teachings of Bhadatta: that which was stated [by him] regarding the first [ascendant] is different.

(Vaṃśastha meter) However, in this system, the *bha* (the sign occupied by the lord of the ascendant) bestows results equal to its own portion, while the *horā* (the first half of the ascendant), being endowed with strength, bestows results equal to the entire sign.
Furthermore, in the case of a malefic rising, there is no *upacaya* (beneficial placement); nor is there any need for the years previously taught for the first [ascendant]. (Indravajrā meter)
In this matter, instruction in truth is best; yet many groups perform what is improper through their numerous assemblies.
While the office of a teacher involves much destruction, that alone which is abundant should be performed.
When Cancer is the ascendant conjoined with Jupiter and the Moon, and Venus and Mercury have gone to a quadrant.

The remaining [planets], including the natural enemies of the house of existence (the Sun), would cause an immeasurable lifespan here to be lost through successive stages. (Puṣpitāgrā) The ten sub-periods (antardaśās) situated in the ascendant,
the Sun, the Moon, the vital points (prāṇa), the quadrants (kendras), and so forth, yield their fruits in the first, middle, and final stages of life.

Indeed, there is no lack of fruition; for the ripening of results occurs first from planets situated in angles (kendras), and even from those in succedent houses (āpoklimas). (Malinī) The lifespan is determined by whichever [factor] is most powerful; its period (daśā) should be assigned first. In case of equality among many [factors], that of the one with the most years is taken; and if there is equality among those as well, that of the one which rose first [is taken]. (Indravajrā)
A planet situated in its own sign gives one-half of its fruit; one in a trine house gives one-third; one in the seventh house gives one-fourth;
and one in a quadrangle gives one-eighth. Thus, when planets occupy one another's houses, they mutually ripen their results.
Having adjusted these [factors] according to their positions and being free from any subtractions below, all of them are to be combined.

The multipliers for the ten-year periods are the [planetary] strengths according to their respective degrees; the divisor is the sum of those [multipliers]. Thus is the division of the ten years. (Indravajrā) A period is fully effective when a planet is correctly strong in its own or exaltation portion; it is void when devoid of strength;
and when situated in its debilitation portion or inimical portion, the period at birth should be known as yielding unfavorable results. (Vaitālīya)

For one fallen from a high point, that which is known as "descending" (avarohinī) is middling when [the planet] is in its friend's exaltation; it is "ascending" (ārohiṇī) for one who has not fallen from a low point. When situated in the degrees of its debilitation, enemy signs, or enemy navāṃśas, it becomes "lowest" (adhamā). For one situated in its debilitation, enemy signs, or enemy navāṃśas, yet in an auspicious house, a mixed result is prescribed for each house.
Now I shall describe their periods (daśās) according to their utility, corresponding to their names.
(Upajātikā meter) In movable signs, both [the lords of the decan and the sign] are considered low, middling, and exalted by the decans respectively;
in fixed signs, they are unfavorable, favorable, and equal respectively. This is the period of the malefic as it is calculated. (Vaitālīya meter)

One, two, nine, twenty, forty, fifty, and sixty are the years for these [planets]—the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, Saturn, and Rāhu—respectively. Their results are nourished by their own [signs] produced at birth. In the sequence of the *daśās*, the *lagna-daśā* is auspicious at the end; thus some Yavanas do not accept it [as the first]. (Śā.vi. When the lord of the *pāka* (maturity) is in the ascendant, or in a friendly division (*varga*), or even with a benefic, the commenced *daśā* bestows auspiciousness; or when the lord of the *pāka* is in the third, tenth, or eleventh house.

When the Moon is situated in the houses of friends, exaltation, *upacaya*, trines, or the seventh house from the lord of the *pāka* (the year), it produces good results; otherwise, it brings evils. (Śāravi) The period (*daśā*) of the Moon, when it has commenced, brings honor, wealth, and happiness if it is in its own house. In the house of Mars, it vitiates one's wife; in the house of Mercury, it bestows knowledge, friends, and wealth.
In the houses of Leo or Scorpio, it provides food; in Capricorn or Aquarius, it gives a wicked wife. In the house of Jupiter, it brings honor, wealth, and happiness. (Śāravi)

Under the Sun (Sūrya), there is injury from one's own nails, teeth, skin, gold, cruelty, travel, kings, and battle; sharpness, courage, constant exertion, delight in effort, fame, majesty, and exaltation;

yet also misfortunes arising from wife, son, wealth, enemies, weapons, fire, and kings; as well as wastefulness, addiction to sin, quarrels with one's own servants, and diseases causing pain in the heart and belly.

Having reached the period of the Moon (Indu), one obtains fruits through mantras, the twice-born, and their origins; through sugarcane, milk products, clothing, flowers, play, sesame, food, and labor.

Excessive sleep, laziness, weak teeth, fondness for gods, birth as a woman, lack of intelligence, loss of fame and wealth, and enmity with one's own kinsmen—these result from [the sub-period of] Mars.
(Śāravi) Crushing of enemies, wealth from kings, brothers, land, sheep, and goats; hatred toward sons, friends, wife, and siblings; hostility toward the learned and gurus;

diseases arising from thirst, blood, fever, bile, and physical breakdown; attachment to the wives of others; delight in sinful acts, devotion to unrighteousness, and harshness and cruelty—these are the results of [the sub-period of] Mars. (Śāravi)
In Baudhī, there is the acquisition of messengership, friends, teachers, twice-born, wealth, praise from the learned, fame, logic, materials,

gold, horses, land, good fortune, happiness, laughter, service, skill, an accumulation of intellect, success in religious acts, harshness, fatigue, bondage, mental grief, and suffering arising from the three humors.
In Jaivī, there is the rise of honor and virtues, an accumulation of intellect, beauty, majesty, exaltation, greatness, effort, political wisdom, wealth through kings, self-study, and mantras.

Gold, horses, sons, elephants, heaps of garments, and affection with virtuous kings; subtlety, reasoning, and a life in the dense forest; hearing, pain, and enmity with those who follow false doctrines.

(Śārṅgadharapaddhati 108) Delight in singing at Śaukya; joy, fragrant substances, food, drink, clothing, women, jewels, splendor, the paraphernalia of Love, knowledge, and the arrival of dear friends;

skill in buying and selling, the acquisition of crops and treasures, and the influx of wealth; enmity with groups, lords of the earth, Niṣādas, and those devoid of dharma; and grief arising from affection. (Śārṅgadharapaddhati 109)
Having reached the period of Saturn, one obtains donkeys, camels, birds, female buffaloes, and old women; honor bestowed by guilds, villages, cities, and officials; the acquisition of inferior grain;

and suffers from phlegm, envy, wind-disorders, delusion, impurity, misfortune, lethargy, and exhaustion. One also faces the rebuking of servants, children, and wife, and incurs physical deformity. (Śāravi) In auspicious periods, they produce beneficial results, while in those designated as inauspicious, they likewise produce their own unfavorable effects.
In the mixed [periods], the results of the sub-periods (niśrā), the results of the decan (daśā), the results of the horā, and those of the lord of the ascendant are equal.

Whatever action, livelihood, or fame was assigned to a planet in the chapter on designations (saṃjñā), as well as that arising from its placement in a house, its aspect, or its conjunction—all of that should be applied to its period (daśā). (Upajātikā and Śālinī meters)
Having reached their own periods, all [the elements] manifest the shadow produced by the great elements;
and from the nose, mouth, eyes, skin, and ears, one may infer the qualities born of water, fire, air, and space.
(Indravajrā) In a period that yields auspicious results, the inner self likewise produces for men much friendship and the arrival of wealth.

One should infer the present [state] by means of the ripened fruits that have been described; the attainment of the fruit matures through dreams, thoughts, and one's own karmic seeds. (Mālinī) When there is a conflict between two similar fruits of a single planet, one should declare the destruction [of the former]; whichever is more predominant is what will ripen. One planet does not destroy the similar fruit of another; having entered their respective periods (*daśā*), they bestow their own fruits. (Vasantatilakā) E8
From its own sign, the Sun goes to the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th, 2nd, 10th, and 7th houses; from Mars, it is exactly the same; from Saturn, to the 7th, 12th, and 6th;

from Venus, to the 7th, 12th, and 6th; from Jupiter, to the 9th, 5th, 11th, and 6th; from the Moon, to the 10th, 3rd, 11th, and 6th; and from Mercury, to the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th, and 12th houses. (Śāravi)

From the Ascendant (Lagna), the Moon is auspicious when situated in the 6th, 3rd, 10th, or 11th houses; from itself, in the 7th, 8th, and so on, up to the 8th and 7th; and from the Sun, in the 6th, 3rd, 11th, or 5th houses. From Mercury (Śaśija), it is auspicious in the 5th, 3rd, 11th, or 8th houses (the *kaṇṭakas*). From Jupiter (Jīva), it is auspicious when occupying the 12th, 11th, 8th, or a quadrant (*kendrastha*). From Venus (Sita), however, it is auspicious when located in the 9th, 4th, 5th, 3rd, 11th, 1st, or 7th houses. But Mars (Vakra) is auspicious from the Sun in the *upacaya* houses, from the Ascendant in the 5th and higher houses, from the Moon in the 10th, 12th, and 11th houses, and from itself in the quadrants, the 8th, the 11th, or the 2nd house. (Śāravi)

From Saturn, [the planet] is auspicious in the 8th, 1st, and 4th houses; from Mercury, in the 6th, 3rd, 5th, and 11th; from Venus, in the 6th, 12th, 11th, and 8th; and from Jupiter, in the 10th, 11th, 3rd, and 6th houses. (Śāravi) From Venus, [the planet] is auspicious in the 2nd, 1st, 11th, 8th, 6th, and 4th houses; from Mars, in the 3rd, 1st, and 5th; from the Moon, in the 9th, 7th, and 6th; from Saturn, in the 12th, 6th, 11th, and 8th; from Jupiter, in the 9th, 11th, 6th, and 12th; from the Sun, in the 9th, 11th, 6th, and 12th; from the Moon, in the 2nd, 1st, 10th, 3rd, 6th, 1st, 11th, 8th, and 4th houses; and from the Ascendant, in the 1st, 11th, 10th, 3rd, 6th, 1st, 11th, 8th, and 4th houses. (Śāravi)

From Mars, Venus is in the 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 9th houses; from the Sun, it is in the 3rd, 5th, 9th, 5th, 2nd, 9th, 10th, 11th, and 6th houses; from Venus, it is in the 7th, 11th, 3rd, 9th, 5th, and 6th houses; from Jupiter, it is in the 4th, 10th, 3rd, 9th, 5th, 1st, 9th, 10th, and 6th houses; from Saturn, it is in the 3rd, 6th, 5th, 12th, 10th, 5th, 6th, 2nd, 4th, 11th, and 1st houses; from Mercury, it is in the 5th, 11th, 8th, 9th, 12th, and 1st houses; and from the Moon, it is in the 2nd, 5th, 11th, 8th, 9th, 12th, and 1st houses. (Śāravi) From the Ascendant, Venus is in the 5th, 11th, 8th, 9th, and 12th houses; from the Moon, it is in the 2nd, 5th, 11th, 8th, 9th, 12th, and 1st houses; from itself, it is in the 5th, 11th, 8th, 9th, 3rd, 5th, 9th, 10th, and 7th houses; and from Saturn, it is in the 4th, 3rd, 5th, 9th, 10th, 7th, and 12th houses.

From the Sun, [the lords of] the eighth, the eleventh, and the twelfth houses are auspicious; from Jupiter, the ninth, the tenth, and the fifth; from Mercury, the fifth, the third, the eleventh, the ninth, the sixth, the fifth, the eleventh, and the twelfth; from Mars, the third, the fifth, the eleventh, and the sixth; from Saturn, the third, the fifth, the eleventh, and the sixth. From Mars, [the lords of] the fourth, the eleventh, the eighth, and the second are auspicious; from the Sun, the third houses; from Mercury, the ninth, the eleventh, the sixth, the twelfth, and the eighth; from the Moon, the third, the sixth, and the eleventh; from Venus, the sixth, the eleventh, and the twelfth; and from Jupiter, the eleventh, the twelfth, the fifth, and the sixth. (Śārṅgadhara-paddhati)
Thus it has been stated: that which is desired is not desired if it differs [from the norm], for a birth with a superior ripening of fruit appears therein; they should grant [the results] there.

That which is desired is strengthened by planets situated in houses of increase, in friendly signs, or in their own or exaltation signs; however, there is no attainment of the desired when they are in houses of decrease, in debilitation, or in inimical signs.
(Mālinī meter) [This concludes the section on] *karma* and *ājīva*.

The attainment of wealth is to be determined by the planets occupying the tenth house from the Sun, the Moon, the Ascendant, or Jupiter—namely, the father, the father’s wife, enemies, friends, brothers, women, the deceased, and so forth.
Furthermore, it depends on the nature of the lord of the ninth house, the lord of the sign occupied by the Moon, and the lord of the navāṃśa occupied by the Sun. (In the Prahārṣiṇī meter:
If the Sun’s portion [is strong], there is gain through grass, gold, water, medicine, and the like; if the Moon’s portion [is strong], it is through agriculture, aquatic products, and women.

In the sub-period (navāṃśa) of Mars, there is success through elements, fire, weapons, and acts of violence; in the sub-period of Mercury, through writing, mathematics, and the like, as well as poetry and arts. (Prahārṣiṇī meter) In the sub-period of Jupiter, there is success through duties such as serving the twice-born and the gods; in the sub-period of Venus, through jewels, silver, and the like, as well as cows and buffaloes. In the sub-period of Saturn, there is success through labor, killing, carrying loads, and lowly crafts; thus, the accomplishment of actions occurs according to the sub-period occupied by the lord of the action. (Prahārṣiṇī meter)

From the planets situated in the houses of friends, enemies, or one's own [Mūlatrikoṇa], wealth is obtained; furthermore, when the Sun is strong and in its exaltation through its own power, and when benefics are placed in the eleventh house or related to the ascendant and the second house, one's own wealth should be considered in many ways according to their strength. (Prahārṣiṇī) E10:
Royal Yoga.

The Yavanas say that when malefic planets are in their own signs or exaltations, the king will be of cruel intellect; however, if there are no malefics, a lord of the earth is not born in the absence of Jupiter's influence. (In Vaitālīya meter) When all three—Mars, Saturn, and the Sun—are in their respective exaltations along with Jupiter, sixteen kings are said to be born in a single ascendant.

Likewise, when one of the two planets situated in the first house is in its own sign and the Moon is present, there shall be sixteen kings. (Vasantatilakā) When the Ascendant or the Moon has reached the highest dignity (Uttamavarga), and is aspected by four or more planets—excluding the Moon—it is recorded that there will be twenty-two kings. (Anuṣṭubh)

When Saturn is in Scorpio, the Sun in Aries, and the Moon in Taurus, with those same planets occupying their respective signs, there is human conjunction; however, if Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are situated in the eighth house, they produce kings. When Saturn and the Moon are in their exaltation signs, the Sun and Mercury are in the sixth house, and Libra, Aries, and the sign of the Moon (Cancer) are occupied by Venus, Mars, and Jupiter, there are kings. When Mars is in its exaltation, the Sun and Moon are in Sagittarius, Saturn is in the ascendant, and another planet is in the seventh house, there is a lord of the earth; likewise, when Mars is in the ascendant along with the Moon, [the others being as described], there is a king.

When the Moon and Saturn are in the seventh house, Jupiter is in Sagittarius, and the Sun has risen in its own exaltation, one becomes a lord of the earth. (Śikhariṇī meter) If Taurus with the Moon is the ascendant, and the Sun, Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn are situated in the fourth, seventh, tenth, and eleventh houses respectively, one invariably becomes a lord of men. If Capricorn with Saturn is the ascendant, and the Moon and the other planets are situated in the third, sixth, ninth, and twelfth houses, one becomes a preeminent leader of men, renowned for his vast virtues and fame. (Śikhariṇī meter)
When Venus, the Moon, and Jupiter are in Leo, Mars is in Capricorn, and Venus and Mercury are in their exaltation signs in the ascendant, there are two kings.

When Saturn and the Sun are in the fifth house, and Jupiter, the Moon, and Venus are in the fourth house while Mercury is in Virgo on the ascendant, one becomes a king; even another person may become so if they possess such qualities.
If the ascendant is Pisces with the Moon, and Saturn, Mars, and the Sun are together in Aquarius, Capricorn, and Leo respectively, that man indeed rules the earth.

If Jupiter is in the sign of Cancer in the ascendant at the time of birth, or if Jupiter is in the ascendant while the preceptor of the gods (Jupiter) is in the sign of Leo, then the native becomes a lord of the earth; otherwise, he becomes a virtuous ruler. (Śikhariṇī meter) If the ascendant is Cancer with Jupiter situated therein, and the Moon, Venus, and Mercury have reached the eleventh house while the Sun is in Aries, one should know that the person born is a lord of the earth endowed with valor. (Vidyunmālā meter)
If Saturn is situated in the ascendant in Capricorn, and Aries, Cancer, and Leo are occupied by their respective lords;
and Mercury and Venus are joined with Gemini and Libra, then one becomes a lord of the earth of great renown. (In the Drutavilambitā meter:
When Mercury is in its own exaltation in the ascendant, and Venus is situated in Aries or Sagittarius...

When Jupiter is in the seventh house, the Moon is in the eighth, and Saturn is in the fifth, even men born of a base family become partakers of sovereignty, let alone those born of royal lineage through the aforementioned planetary configurations for kings.
Those born of a royal family become monarchs by the configurations to be described hereafter; among them, one who has no royal father becomes equal to a king.
When the planets are in their exaltations, own signs, or trines, and are strong, those born of royal lineages become lords of men;

those born of other lineages with five or more [planets so situated] become wealthy, but if they are weak, they are not protectors of the earth. (Aupacchandasika meter) When the Sun is in the tenth house, the Moon in the first, Mars in its exaltation in Aries, and Saturn in Aquarius;

When Jupiter has reached the sign of Sagittarius (Cāpa), one should know that the king will obtain a son who is a lord of the earth. (Vidyunmālā) When Venus is in its own asterism, the Moon has reached the seventh house (Pātāla), and the remaining planets have attained the third and first houses (Duścikya and Aṅga), the one born becomes the sovereign of the earth. (Vidyunmālā)

When Mercury is endowed with strength and occupies the ascendant, and a benefic planet, rich in strength, is situated in a house of fortune, wealth, or gain, while the remaining planets are in their respective positions, one born of a king becomes a lord of the earth— a righteous soul (Navamālikā). When Taurus rises, and the Moon, Jupiter, Saturn, and the others occupy the first, second, sixth, and eleventh houses respectively, one becomes a king.

If Jupiter is in the fourth house, the Moon in the tenth, and the Sun in the seventh, while the other planets are in the eleventh house, one becomes a king. (Vaṃśastha meter) If the Moon, Saturn, and Jupiter are in the ascendant, Mercury and Mars are in the second house, Venus and the Sun are in the fourth house, and Rahu and Ketu are in the tenth house, one attains lordship over men. (Vasnatatilakā meter)
During the ripening period (pākadaśā) of the lord of the natal ascendant (karmalagna), there is the attainment of royalty, or else [it occurs] during that of a powerful planet.
During the period of one situated in an enemy's sign or its fall (nīca), the period of one occupying a vulnerable point (chidra) should be considered. (To oneself:

When Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury are in the ascendant, Saturn is in the seventh house, and the Sun is in the sky (the tenth house), one should know that this is the birth of those who enjoy pleasures.

When the Kendras are joined by auspicious planets and the malefics are situated in the [other] houses, one attains the status of a Śabara chief or a bandit leader and becomes a possessor of wealth. (Mālinī meter) E11.
The Nabhasa yogas, multiplied by nine, ten, eight, three, three, and four respectively, arise from the two, three, and four-fold combinations.
That [total] of six hundred multiplied by three is said to be the extent in detail; the others are equal to that.
(Aupacchandasika) The *rajju*, *muśala*, *nala*, *cara*, and so forth, along with *satya* and *āśrayaja* through their respective combinations, are called the "half-named" (*dalākhya*).
When joined with the planets in the quadrants (*kendras*) as favorable or unfavorable, they are described by Parāśara as the *srak* (garland) and *sarpa* (serpent). (Aupacchandasika)
"Yogas arising from the [planetary] positions attain equality with barley, lotus, thunderbolt, egg-born, ball, and so forth, when they occupy the angles (kendras).
Others say that the two known as 'half' (dala), which have the aforementioned results, do not produce separate results [when in other houses].

(Upajātikā meter) When planets occupy the two houses nearest to the angle, it is called the "mace" (gadā); when they are in the ascendant and the seventh house, it is the "cart" (śakaṭa); and when they are in the fourth and tenth houses, it is the "bird" (vihaga).

Those who know [astrology] declare that when the [planets] are situated in the ninth, fifth, and the ascendant (lagna), while being elsewhere than the ascendant, it is "Śṛṅgāṭaka"; they call it "Hala" when [the planets] are situated in other houses than the ascendant.
Like the cart and the bird, it is auspicious or inauspicious; "Vajra" occurs when they are situated in those same houses, and "Yava" when they are situated in the opposite ones.

If the *kamala* [meter] is formed by the arrangement of mixed [syllables], or if it is situated outside the *kendra* [positions]—(in the *vaitālīyā* meter)—I have composed the *vajra* and other [meters] according to the previous treatises.
How can Mercury and Venus be located in the fourth house from the Sun? (in the *anuṣṭubh* meter).

When the planets are situated in the four houses starting from the ascendant (the *kaṇṭakas*), they form, respectively, the *yūpa*, *śakti*, and *daṇḍa* configurations, as well as the *horā* and others, by means of the *kaṇṭakas*. Similarly, when they are situated in the seven constellations [starting from Aśvinī], they form the *nau* (boat), *kūṭa* (peak), *chatra* (umbrella), and *cāpa* (bow) configurations.
The "Half-moon" (ardhacandra) configuration is said to occur when [planets] are situated in other asterisms starting from the third house;
the "Ocean" (samudra) occurs when they are situated in houses six apart;
and the "Wheel" (cakra) occurs when they are situated starting from the ascendant (lagna). This is the summary of configurations based on their shapes.

There are seven combinations of numbers based on the positions of the seven planets: Vallakī, Dāminī, Pāśa, Kedāra, Śūlayoga, Yuga, and Gola—excluding those previously mentioned. (In the Śālinī meter:
One born under the *rajjuyoga* is envious, intent on foreign lands, and fond of travel; one born under the *muśalayoga* is proud, wealthy, and devoted to many tasks.

One born under Nala is deformed but firm, wealthy, and skillful; one born from Sraṅga is endowed with enjoyments; and one born under Bhujaga shall experience much suffering. (Vaṃti) Those [planets] mentioned as providing support become fruitless when mixed with others;
those by which they are mixed will yield their own results, while unmixed ones grant their specific fruits. (Anuṣṭubh)

In Gadā, one is a performer of sacrifices, a recipient of wealth, and constantly delights in material gain; the son born under Śakaṭa suffers from disease and has a wicked wife; one born in Dūta wanders about, creates quarrels, and is declared to be like a bird; in Śṛṅgāṭaka, one enjoys long-lasting happiness; and in Dhvaja, one is a farmer and possesses eyes like a plowshare.
(Va-ti) In Vajra, those who are last or first enjoy happiness; one is fortunate, exceedingly brave, and endowed with valor; furthermore, in Yava, one is happy until the end of life.
In Padma, he is of renowned fame, possessing immeasurable happiness and virtues, with a firm and stable body; he is a provider of wealth but not a giver.
(Va-ti) He is generous and self-possessed, and performs sacrifices with the best of rituals; in Yūpa, he is indeed cruel and appointed as a guardian. In Śara, he is a maker of arrows.
(Va-ti) In Śakti, he is base, lazy, and deprived of happiness and wealth; in Daṇḍa, he is separated from loved ones and subsists on the lowest of occupations. (Va-ti)
One born in the *kūṭa* of Mercury is endowed with fame, possesses fickle happiness, and is miserly; he is devoid of vigor and is subject to falsehood, floating, and imprisonment.

One born in the *kūṭa* of Jupiter brings happiness to his own kin, finds happiness at the end of his life, and is brave. One born in the *kūṭa* of Venus finds happiness at the beginning and at the end.
One born in the *kūṭa* of the Moon is fortunate, possesses a lovely body, is preeminent, and like a lord of men, enjoys pleasures in a watery abode.
One born under Cakra has feet adorned by the luster of the crowns of lords of men; one born under Vīṇā is skillful and fond of song and dance.
(Va.Ti) One born under Dātṛ is intent on other tasks; one born under Paśu is bound by a rope and a noose. One born under Dhana is devoid of virtue, possessing servants and kinsmen.
One born under Kedāra is a farmer, highly useful, and brave. One born under Kṣata desires wealth but is impoverished. One born under Śūla is likewise destitute. (Va.Ti)

Devoid of wealth, a heretic, or born in the Golaka yoga during this age; lacking resources, impure yet possessed of knowledge; a poor artisan, lazy, and wandering—thus have been described here the Nabhasa yogas along with their fruits. These are to be considered as yielding certain results throughout all planetary periods (daśās). (Hariṇī meter) E12 Candrayoga.

When the Moon is situated in the fourth, tenth, or first house from the Sun's exaltation sign (arka-kendra), there arise discipline, wealth, knowledge, intellect, and skill; these qualities are found in the day or night according to the Moon's state. If the Moon is in its own or a highly friendly Navamsha, or is aspected by Jupiter and Venus, one shall be wealthy and happy. When the Moon forms an Adhiyoga with benefics in the seventh, sixth, or eighth houses, that birth is that of an army commander, a minister, or a protector of the earth.

Those born with the Moon in a *sunaphā*, *anaphā*, or *durudhurā* yoga—formed by planets situated in its own, twelfth, or both (eighth and second) houses—become endowed with abundant happiness and wealth, have their enemies destroyed, enjoy long lives, and are free from disease and fear.

(*Vṛtta-taraṅgiṇī*) Excluding the Sun, when the Moon is in a *kemadruma* yoga due to many other planets being placed elsewhere [than the aforementioned], it is so described; however, others say this is not the case. Some maintain that if the Moon is in a quadrant (*kendram*) or conjoined with a planet, a *kemadruma* is not desired. Others say it occurs when the Moon is in a quadrant or a ninth-part (*navāṃśaka*), but those [latter views] are not well-known traditional teachings. (*Śārṅgadhara-paddhati*)
There are thirty varieties known as *sārūpa*, *sunaphā*, and *anaphā*, and ninety-three divisions of *daurudhura*.

Having sequentially applied these according to one's desires and variations, there is cessation, and then another method follows. (*Indravajrā*) Indeed, in *sunaphā*, one becomes a king who has acquired wealth by himself, or one equal to a king, possessing intelligence, wealth, and fame.
In Anaphā, one possesses a body free from disease, is virtuous, renowned for fame, enjoys sensual pleasures, is well-dressed, and is contented.

(Mālinī meter) In Kemadruma, one experiences the arising of wealth, vehicles, and the enjoyment of produced pleasures; one is endowed with generosity, possesses excellent servants, and is capable of bearing heavy burdens.
However, those born under Kemadruma—even if of royal lineage—become dirty, miserable, base, destitute, servile, and wicked. (Vaṃśastha meter)
The son of Earth (Mars) possesses energy, valor, wealth, and daring; he is gentle, clever, eloquent, and skilled in the arts.
Jupiter enjoys wealth, virtue, and pleasure, and is honored by kings. Venus is lustful and possesses great wealth, being a connoisseur of sensual objects.
Saturn is an enjoyer of the riches and retinues of others, performing many tasks, and is a leader among the hosts.

The Moon that performs inauspicious acts has its form visible during the day; the auspicious Moon has its form dissolved. The rest is to be inferred otherwise. (Puṣpitāgrā meter) One is exceedingly wealthy from the Ascendant (Lagna), and wealthy from the Moon (Śaśāṅka), when all the benefic planets occupy their positions of increase (Upacaya).

One is equal [to the wealthy] with two [benefics], and possesses little wealth when they are fewer than that. Even if other results are absent, this [result] prevails by virtue of its intensity. (Vaṃśasthavila meter) E13

In a dual-planet yoga, the Sun, joined by Venus, produces a man who works with machines and stones; with Mars, one who is base; with Mercury, one who is skillful, endowed with wisdom, fame, and happiness;

with Jupiter, one who is cruel and devoted to other pursuits; with Venus, one who has acquired wealth through the stage or weapons; and with Saturn, one skilled in minerals or in various types of crafts. (Śāravi)

If Venus is in the seventh house, the native deals in counterfeit goods, women, intoxicants, and jars; he is inauspicious and crooked toward his mother. If Mercury is there, he speaks with humility, is skilled in matters of profit, endowed with good fortune and fame, valiant, a leader of his family, yet unstable in mind and a lord of wealth. If Jupiter is there, he is a master of garments and skilled in rituals and other such activities. If Saturn is there, he is the son of a remarried woman. (Śāravi) If Mercury is in the seventh house, the native is a merchant who trades in roots and the like, as well as oils and counterfeit items, and is a fighter with his arms. If Jupiter is there, he becomes a city superintendent, or a king, or a Brahmin who has acquired great wealth.

If Jupiter is in the sign of Aries (Mesa), the native will be a cowherd, a wrestler, clever, devoted to other women, a gambler, and under the influence of the chief of Asuras; he will be afflicted by suffering and false to his word. If in Taurus (Vrishabha), he will be censured by his father. (Shatpada-vishama) If joined with Mercury, he will be a stage-player; if joined with Jupiter, he will be fond of song, skilled in dance, eloquent, and a leader of the earth's people. If joined with Venus, he will be gentle, clever in magic, and a jumper.

If joined with Saturn, he should be known as one possessed of true learning, wealth, and a wife, endowed with many virtues; or else, if born [with these configurations], he will be a barber, a potter, or a maker of food. (Shalini-vishama)
When there is a conjunction of dark and light [planets], one who has little vision gains wealth through association with young women;

he becomes a knower of scripts, books, and paintings. The results described by others are to be considered according to these [specific] indications. (Puṣpitāgrā meter) E14 Pravrajyāyoga (The Yoga of Renunciation)

Those born when four or more planets are situated in one sign, endowed with strength and occupying their respective houses of valor (vīryagatas), become Śākyas, Ājīvikas, Bhikṣus, Vṛddhas, Carakas, Nirgranthas, or forest-dwelling ascetics. Respectively, through the influence of Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, the Moon, Venus, and Saturn, there is renunciation (pravrajyā) when they are strong; if they are defeated by their own lords, there is a fall from that state. When the Sun is strong, men who have not been initiated (adīkṣitas) but possess devotion toward him [the Sun] are born. When the Moon is strong, those devoted to him [the Moon] are born. When Mars is strong, those devoted to him [Mars] are born. When Mercury is strong, those devoted to him [Mercury] are born. When Jupiter is strong, those devoted to him [Jupiter] are born. When Venus is strong, those devoted to him [Venus] are born. When Saturn is strong, those devoted to him [Saturn] are born.

When the Moon is aspected by Saturn while situated in the portion of Mars, and is conjoined with Saturn in the first house, one obtains initiation (dīkṣā) from those who have been initiated merely upon request and are slain even while being watched by others.

(Vaitālīya) If the lord of the birth [the Moon] is not seen by others, and Saturn aspects the son of the Sun (Mars), or the lord of the birth is weak in strength, one receives initiation when the Moon is in the aspect of Saturn, situated in the portion of Mars, and aspected by Saturn. (Mālinī)
When Jupiter is aspected by Jupiter, the Moon, the Ascendant, Mars, and the Sun in the ninth house, he becomes a king born through a yoga and a performer of sacred rites (tīrthakṛt).
When Saturn is situated in the ninth house and aspected by other planets, there occurs the "King Yoga," and he becomes an anointed lord of men.
(Nakṣatra-phala)
One born under the Aśvinī constellation is fond of ornaments, handsome, fortunate, skillful, and wise.
One born under the Bharaṇī constellation is firm in resolve, truthful, free from disease, capable, and happy.
One born under the Kṛttikā constellation is a great eater, devoted to the wives of others, radiant, and famous.
Under Rohiṇī, one is truthful, pure, pleasant-spoken, steady-minded, and handsome.
(Āryā) Under Mṛgaśiras, one is fickle, clever, timid, skillful, energetic, wealthy, and an enjoyer of pleasures.
Under Ārdrā, one is indeed deceitful, arrogant, ungrateful, violent, sinful, and fierce. (Āryā)

A man born under Punarvasu is self-controlled, happy, virtuous, yet dull-witted, prone to disease, and thirsty; he is satisfied with very little. (Āryā verse) One born under Puṣya has a tranquil soul, is fortunate, learned, wealthy, and devoted to righteousness.
In Śaṭha, one is deceitful, a consumer of all things, sinful, ungrateful, and a rogue;
in Bhaujaṅga, one has many servants, wealth, and enjoyments, is devoted to the gods and ancestors, and possesses great effort.
In Pitrya, one is pleasant-spoken, generous, radiant, a wanderer, and a servant of kings; in Bhāgya, these same qualities apply. (Āryā verses)
One born under the second Phālgunī is fortunate, has acquired wealth through knowledge, enjoys pleasures, and partakes in happiness.
One born under Hasta is energetic, bold, a drinker, compassionate, and a thief.
Under Citrā, one wears variegated garments and garlands, possesses beautiful eyes, and has a handsome body.
One who is self-controlled, a merchant, compassionate, pleasant-spoken, and devoted to righteousness is born under Svāti.
(Āryā meter) One who is envious, greedy, radiant, eloquent, and quarrelsome is born under Viśākhā.
One who is wealthy, a dweller in foreign lands, hungry, and a wanderer is born under Anurādhā. (Āryā meter)
Under Jyeṣṭhā, one has many friends, is contented, performs dharma, and possesses great anger.
Under Mūla, one is honorable, wealthy, happy, non-violent, steady, and an enjoyer of pleasures.
Under the water-deity (Pūrvāṣāḍhā), one has beloved and joyful wives, is honorable, and possesses firm friendship.
Under the *Viśvadevas*, one is well-trained, righteous, has many friends, is grateful, and fortunate.
(Āryā meter) Under *Śravaṇa*, one is illustrious, learned, noble in wife, endowed with wealth, famous, generous, wealthy, brave, fond of song, and greedy for riches. (Āryā meter)
In Śatabhiṣaj, one is eloquent, addicted to vice, a slayer of enemies, and reckless;
in the Bhādrapadas, one is difficult to restrain, belongs to two groups, is dominated by women, wealthy, clever, and a non-giver.
(Āryā verse) In the second [nakṣatra], one is an orator, happy, possessed of offspring, a conqueror of foes, and righteous.
In the [sub-period] of Puṣan, one is complete in limb, fortunate, heroic, pure, and wealthy.

(Āryā verse) One born under the Moon [sign] has the character and conduct of the lunar mansions; his eyes are copper-colored, he eats warm food, vegetables, and light meals, and he is quick to show favor. He is a wanderer, lustful, with weak knees, unstable wealth, heroic, and beloved by women.

One born in the *Kriyā* (Taurus) *navāṃśa* is a servant, possesses calluses on the feet, has scars from wounds on his head, is proud, rises with his elder brother, has a mark on the palm of his hand, is extremely fickle, and is very timid in water.

(Śārṅgadharapaddhati) One born in the *Go* (Taurus) *navāṃśa* is beloved, has a playful gait, broad thighs and face, is marked on the back, mouth, and sides, is generous, endures hardship, is a leader, has a hump, has daughters as offspring, is phlegmatic (*śleṣmala*), is separated from paternal kinsmen, wealth, and sons, is endowed with good fortune, is patient, has a bright digestive fire, is dear to women, has stable friends, and finds happiness in middle age and at the end of life. (Śārṅgadharapaddhati)

When the Moon is in the third lunar mansion (Ārdrā), the messenger is lustful toward women, skilled in the arts of lovemaking, copper-hued in his eyes, learned in the scriptures, curly-haired, sharp-witted, and knowledgeable in laughter, gestures, and gambling; he possesses beautiful limbs, speaks kindly, delights in splendor and fragrances, loves song, and is skilled in dance—such a man with a prominent nose finds pleasure with eunuchs.

When the Moon is like that [in the fourth mansion], the messenger moves straight and swiftly, has a prominent hip, is overcome by women, is a true friend, and is a knower of the divine (or astrology); he is endowed with abundant dwellings, destruction of enemies, and wealth.

A man born under the Moon (Śaśāṅka) is short of stature, has a thick neck, and is fond of his kinsmen; he is affectionate toward friends, delights in water and gardens, and is devoted to his own home.

(Śārṅgadharapaddhati 105) One born in the Sun’s asterism (Sūryabhā) is sharp-witted, has large jaws and a broad face, with tawny eyes and few children; he hates women, loves meat and forest trees, and remains angry for a long time over a slight offense.
Afflicted by hunger, thirst, stomach ailments, dental pain, and mental distress, yet generous, valiant, steady-minded, proud, and obedient to his mother. (Śārṅgadharapaddhati 106)

With a charming gait and glances slow with modesty, his shoulders drooping and arms long, he is happy, gentle, devoted to truth, skilled in the arts, conversant with the meaning of the scriptures, and righteous. Intelligent and fond of sexual pleasure, he is endowed with the houses and wealth of others; if born as a daughter, she will travel to a foreign land, be sweet-spoken, have daughters as offspring, and few sons. (Śārṅgadharasaṃhitā) Devoted to honoring gods, Brahmins, and the virtuous, wise, pure, yet dominated by women, tall, with a prominent nose, with thin and tremulous limbs, wandering, and possessed of wealth.

One born in Scorpio has deficient limbs, is skilled in buying and selling, possesses two names, and provides assistance to his kinsmen; yet, having been offended by them, he is abandoned by them in the seventh year.
(Śārdūlavikrīḍita) The one born in Libra has broad eyes and chest, rounded calves, thighs, and knees; he is separated from his father and preceptor in childhood and is afflicted by disease.
Honored in the royal family, tawny-complexioned, and of cruel disposition, he conceals his sins with the signs of the fish, thunderbolt, bird, and goad. (Mālinī)

One born under Vyāghāta has a long face and head, inherits paternal wealth, is renunciant, a poet, and heroic; he is eloquent, has large teeth, ears, lower lip, and nose, is industrious, and skilled in the arts;

he is hunchbacked at the shoulders, has deformed nails, symmetrical shoulders and arms, is bold, knows the Dharma, is hostile toward kinsmen, does not yield to force, can be won over only by lineage or conciliation, and is born from a horse. (Śāravi) One born under Śatabhiṣaj always fondles his own wife and children, bears the banner of righteousness, is thin below, has beautiful eyes, a slender waist, is firm in speech, possesses good fortune, and is indolent.

In Capricorn, a man is fond of cold things, a wanderer, and preponderantly passionate; he is a poet, greedy, devoted to forbidden women and the aged, shameless, and devoid of pity. (Śārdūlavikrīḍita) He has a neck like a camel's, is veiny, with a rough, hairy, and long body, and possesses broad feet, thighs, back, hips, face, and waist; he is aged.
